main_statement.latex: \begin{theorem}[Uniform boundedness] For each integer d>=1, there is a finite nonnegative integer B(d) such that every real planar polynomial vector field of degree at most d has at most B(d) limit cycles in the whole plane. \end{theorem}  ||  \begin{theorem} If deg F<=5, the system x'=y-F(x), y'=-x has at most two limit cycles in R^2. Some members of this class have two limit cycles. Thus its exact maximum is two. \end{theorem}
main_statement.paraphrase: 143a (headline, NOT formalized): for each degree d there is a finite B(d) bounding the number of limit cycles of every planar polynomial vector field of degree <= d (existential part of Hilbert's 16th problem), non-effective. 143b (formalized, comparator OAI.QuinticLienard.main): every classical Lienard system x'=y-F(x), y'=-x with deg F <= 5 has at most 2 limit cycles and 2 is attained (degree-5 case of the Lins-de Melo-Pugh conjecture).

comparator.theorem: OAI.QuinticLienard.main : (forall F : Polynomial R, F.degree <= 5 -> {C : Set Plane | IsLimitCycle F C}.encard <= 2) and (exists F : Polynomial R, F.degree <= 5 and {C | IsLimitCycle F C}.encard = 2)
comparator.model: vectorField F (x,y) = (y - F.eval x, -x); IsSolution: global C^1 solution on all of R (HasDerivAt at every t); IsPeriodicOrbit C: exists solution z, T>0, z T-periodic, z nonconstant, C = range z; IsLimitCycle C: periodic orbit with an open U containing C such that every periodic orbit C' contained in U equals C. Count = Set.encard (ENat), so infinitely many cycles would also be excluded.

main_statement.match_check: 143b: exact. Comparator defs (QuinticLienard.lean:7-23) are textually identical to solution Model.lean:7-23; Main.lean:20-23 proves `main` as <upper_bound, Sharpness.sharpness>. Isolation notion = 'some neighbourhood containing no other whole periodic orbit', identical to paper's introduction.tex:7-11; geometric count without multiplicity; F of degree <=5 including degenerate/constant F (paper first normalizes F(0)=0 by shifting y; Lean instead carries the constant term poly a 0 through the matching, CycleIsolation.lean:26, and makes the x^5 coefficient nonnegative via the homeomorphism flipY with F -> -F, CycleTransform.lean:54-59). The family's headline result (Hilbert 16 uniform bound) therefore rests on an unrefereed, unformalized paper; the Lean-backed result is the far narrower LMP degree-5 case.

paraphrase_by_manuscript.143a: Existential (uniform) part of Hilbert's 16th problem: for each degree d the Hilbert number H(d) is finite. Non-effective; no formula for B(d). Limit cycles counted geometrically, no hyperbolicity or genericity assumption, no use of individual finiteness (Ilyashenko-Ecalle) as a premise.
paraphrase_by_manuscript.143b: Lins Neto-de Melo-Pugh conjecture in degree 5: every classical Lienard system with polynomial F of degree <=5 (no parity/sign restriction) has at most 2 limit cycles, and 2 is attained. Previously known: odd quintic (Rychkov 1975), quartic (Li-Llibre 2012), slow-fast cyclicity <=2 (Li-Lu 2014); conjecture false for n>=6.

Errors, if any, most likely sit in the uniformity-per-finite-request quantifiers of Secs 3-8 and in the retestability (germ invariance) of the primitive packets.
